visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from the facility's licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

Virginia opossum, adult, admitted in February after being found in an unheated outbuilding. Severe frostbite of all four feet and the distal tail. Necrotic tissue has demarcated and sloughed over five weeks; the animal has lost the distal portions of all four feet and approximately 60% of the tail. Wounds are fully healed with stable scar tissue.

Animal is in good body condition, eating well, ambulatory on the healed stumps, and grooming normally. No pain behaviors and no analgesia required for three weeks. Attending veterinarian assessed Five Domains as acceptable.

Animal is non-releasable: it cannot climb, cannot grip with the tail, and cannot dig or forage effectively. Opossums in this region depend on climbing to escape predators.

Placement: opossums are occasionally used as education animals; a permitted facility with lawful authorization has confirmed placement for this animal notwithstanding the limb loss. No breeding or research use.

Permanent captivity would require ground-level caging with soft substrate and daily care. Virginia opossums are short-lived; expected remaining captive lifespan is approximately 18 months to 2 years.
menu_options: Continue care for the animal's remaining lifespan
Transfer the animal to another facility
Release the animal at the original site
